newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares continue downward trend.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares continue downward trend.

text.p: Delhi stocks dipped in afternoon trade on Friday as foreign and domestic institutions booked profits by selling frontline stocks, brokers said.
At 12.45 p.m. (0715 GMT) the Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index was down 10 points to 917.82.
"The fall in share prices is more of a technical correction, as the market had risen sharply on active buying by overseas players," said Bharat Bhushan Aggarwal of brokers Nu-Era Equity.
Traders said stocks of multinational companies continued to face selling pressure for the second straight session and lost further ground.
Bank of India lost 2.75 rupees to 349.
Hindustan Lever Ltd fell 12 rupees to 1,348.
